messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test failure is because ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class) eventually calls ClassUtils.getShortClassName(String) passing the class name obtained via cls.getName(). For array classes, the class name returned by cls.getName() follows the internal JVM notation: it usually starts with one or more '[' characters indicating the number of dimensions, followed by a character denoting the type, and for object types, ends with a semicolon (';'). For example, a String array class name is something like "[Ljava.lang.String;".

The getShortClassName(String) method does not properly handle this array encoding. It does a simple substring operation based on the last '.' character and replaces inner class '$' characters by '.'. This logic is fine for normal classes, but for array types with this JVM internal name format, it will incorrectly treat the trailing semicolon as part of the class name, causing the string output to have an erroneous semicolon suffix. This matches the bug report's description of a semicolon being appended incorrectly for arrays.

Thus, the root cause is the lack of special handling in getShortClassName(String) for array class names in the internal JVM format. The method needs additional logic to parse and decode the array notation properly, converting it into a user-friendly short class name format without semicolons or JVM type encodings.

The failing test confirms this as it expects "String[]" but the method returns "String;" when called with String[].class.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this issue.

Recommended fix:
Add handling for the array internal class name format in getShortClassName(String), decoding array notation and object type markers, stripping semicolons, and formatting the name correctly.
